questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
My destination very much depended on the courses the university would offer - the courses had to match those offered at home.
Besides the courses, the geographic location and appeal of the location also played a significant part in my choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. Overall the whole process up to the travel day was complicated and not as straightforward as you could hope.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I met other students from back home that were able to help, including the International Mobility office in Milan and at home in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. I searched on facebook marketplace among many other sites. I got through to an agency called Dovevivo, can't necessarily recommend them, but they managed to find a place for me. The place had bedbugs, but because it was an agency and not private, they were responsible to helping me find a temporary place to stay while they disinfected the place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's more expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process required our attendance to collect our Erasmus student card. There was not much to that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: International Mobility office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Together with a couple others, we were able to find the appropriate courses, although we had to change one in the beginning. We managed to cover 27 ECTS, leaving us with 3 ECTS remaining. We will make up for those at home by writing an assignment of a specified length of our own interest and choice that will need approval.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do your thorough research from home, and be open to change the course at your arrival if you can already tell a) either it's not in your interest or b) the duration is too long.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: From my perspective, 2 out of the 4 courses I had, met similar standards as at home. These were Time Series Analysis and Game Theory. A significant difference from UCPH and Milan University, was the limited amount of home assignments. As we know from home, these take up a lot of time and require a lot of work. We barely had any of such during our stay.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Less digital than at home - exams were by hand. 

They combined lectures with classroom exercises, although classroom exercises were very limited.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
All courses were trimester courses:
- Times Series Analysis (6 ECTS)
- Game Theory (6 ECTS)
- Business History (6 ECTS)
- New Business Startup (9 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Time Series Analysis and Game Theory

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had a bedbug incident in the beginning of my stay which led to some unexpected costs. Dovevivo (the agency) covered the majority, but I still had to pay for my living costs during my temporary stay outside my apartment.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks were relatively "cheap" considering it's Milan. Also, train tickets to go outside Milan were very cheap in comparison to e.g. Danish train rides.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The usual sports. I tried to sign up for football, but the coach only spoke Italian and we were 200 participants trying out for the Uni team, and they were only letting in 12 players. The chances of getting in, were very slim.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Non

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside Milan for one-day visits to nearby towns/cities. We were also a group that rented a van for 3 days and went on a joyful trip across Italy (from Milan to Padova to Trieste and back). I can highly recommend doing that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Italians are very social and open to Erasmus students. We were often approached by the locals that we studied with. Just like any place, be open and ready to socialise.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Italians barely eat any breakfast and they eat late. I more or less continued my normal eating habits, yet I also tried to adjust a little to try it out.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Italian food, drinks, coffee and late-night evenings.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Enjoy and don't stress out too much - although you may lack information here and there, it usually always works out
2) Go on weekend trips and explore Milan city 
3) Go to San Siro stadium ;)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prior to your trip, ask around in your friend groups if they may know anyone that is doing a similar exchange as you to Milan - I managed to meet some of the first people (that I still socialize with today) when I arrived because of this.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friends, new stories to tell and very little Italian

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Was when I first arrived and knew no one. You had to sightsee the city yourself, eat out by yourself, and entertain yourself. I worked out very well, but got a little challenging and frustrating after just a week.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
